finding: RF012 is real, but the safe repair cannot be a bare comparison against canonical AUTHOR_DECISION.subject_ref. The Author Decision Queue intentionally keeps exact subject identities and concurrency/provenance metadata in its queue ledger and resolution receipt while preserving the legacy canonical AUTHOR_DECISION projection. Content Admission currently receives only canonical parent state plus author_decision_refs, so it lacks sufficient authoritative evidence to prove exact decision applicability.

evidence.queue_rule: A previously committed AUTHOR_DECISION remains immutable history but consumers must independently test whether it is current/applicable to their exact subject before acting.
evidence.canonical_projection_rule: Queue-only identity, provenance and concurrency metadata remain in queue ledger/receipt rather than silently changing the canonical AUTHOR_DECISION schema.

rejected_repairs: Do not infer exact applicability from APPROVED status plus affirmative author_choice alone.
Do not treat canonical AUTHOR_DECISION.subject_ref as a substitute for the queue receipt's exact subject_identity_refs when the decision contract requires exact identity/currentness.
Do not add queue-only metadata silently to the canonical AUTHOR_DECISION schema.
Do not modify the original hosted-passed content-admission subject e993806a1d9a4838d4bd6d162a36921526ef302a in place.
Do not transfer the existing Author Decision Current Subject Guard A-01 PASS to a new content-admission bridge or derivative.

selected_repair_shape.rule: Introduce a narrow adapter around Content Admission that is given authoritative Author Decision Queue evidence by the owning Book parent, verifies the referenced decision and resolution receipt, verifies exact subject-identity applicability/currentness using the already-qualified strict-currentness semantics, then delegates unchanged canonical content admission. The adapter may narrow admission only; it cannot create, choose, approve, resolve, or mutate an AUTHOR_DECISION.
required_inputs: author-decision queue ledger or exact immutable resolution-receipt projection sufficient to resolve the referenced decision
per-author-decision applicability binding that states which exact subject_identity_refs the operation requires
required_checks: every requires_author_decision operation has an explicit applicability binding
binding references one canonical AUTHOR_DECISION already present in parent state
AUTHOR_DECISION status/choice is acceptable to the unchanged Content Admission base contract
an immutable queue resolution receipt resolves to the same decision_id
receipt subject_identity_refs exactly match the binding's required subject identities
those subject identities remain current/applicable under the strict-currentness guard semantics where governed-currentness applies
decision/receipt/binding mismatch fails closed before base content admission can mutate state
failed applicability emits no successful admission receipt and no parent mutation
authority_nonexpansion: no export freeze or publication authority

exact_sha_law.bridge_rule: Any adapter/test implementation receives a new exact subject SHA and requires fresh focused plus full hosted qualification; any later A-01 admission is separately registered and adjudicated.

required_outputs: additive applicability-guard module delegating to unchanged content admission
existing 30-case content-admission regression unchanged and passing
existing Author Decision guard regression unchanged and passing
fresh exact derivative SHA and hosted evidence
next_work_contract.stop_condition: Fail closed rather than implement if exact queue receipt identity/currentness cannot be resolved without widening canonical AUTHOR_DECISION or inventing author evidence.

completion_delta: RF012 now has a contract-compatible repair architecture. The proven gap is no longer routed to an unsafe subject_ref-only patch: the next executable job is a narrow parent-side evidence bridge that preserves the canonical decision schema and all existing exact-SHA qualifications.
